text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- In efforts to reduce rising health insurance premiums, the Swiss government has decided to increase the annual minimum deductible from 150 Swiss francs to 230 francs.
- Union Bank of Switzerland wants to sell its subsidiary Aufina in Brugg, which specialises in consumer credits.

- Swiss Social Minister Ruth Dreifuss has succeeded in efforts to change consitutional laws on maternity leave. The Swiss government approved 14 weeks paid maternity leave for working and non-working women.
- The Swiss government intends to cut subventions for agriculture, transportation and water protection by 229 million Swiss francs.
- Swiss-Swedish engineering group ABB received an order from China to build a power plant for $650 million.
- The Swiss cabinet approved a plan to allow the Swiss National Bank to allocate 100 million Swiss francs to a fund for Holocaust victims.
